title: Validate onboarding step: first successful Hosted API request (per project)
creator: Dylan Brooks
description:
Implement validation logic for the Guided Onboarding checklist step: “Make your first successful API request”.

We need a reliable signal that a given project has made at least one successful request to the Hosted API (any of the supported endpoints) and then mark the checklist step complete for that project.

Context:
- This is used by the Console checklist behind a feature flag.
- Step completion should be computed server-side (source of truth) and exposed via the checklist state API.
- Must be privacy-safe: do not store request bodies/prompt content.

Definition (proposed):
- “First successful request” == first request for a (org_id, project_id) that returns HTTP 2xx from the Redwood API gateway for a model inference endpoint.
- Endpoints included: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank (and any future /v1/* inference routes tagged as inference=true).
- Exclusions: auth failures (401/403), quota/rate limit (429), client errors (4xx non-2xx), server errors (5xx).

Target UX behavior:
- After first success, checklist step flips to “Complete” in Console within ~5–10 minutes (acceptable lag for Phase 1).
acceptance_criteria: For a new project, the checklist step FIRST_SUCCESSFUL_REQUEST transitions to Complete after the first 2xx inference request (any supported endpoint).
Step does NOT complete on 401/403/404/429/5xx responses.
Step completion is per project_id (not global per org).
Validation is idempotent (re-processing logs/events does not create duplicate state changes).
No prompt content or request body is stored or emitted in telemetry; only allowed metadata fields are persisted.
Backfill works for projects that already made a successful request prior to checklist enablement (at least last 30 days).
Unit tests cover endpoint matching, status code filtering, and idempotency behavior.
Emits onboarding telemetry when the step is marked complete (per schema allowlist) for funnel measurement.
implementation_notes:
Decision (per DevEx + Platform discussion): use gateway request logs/metrics as the source of truth for “success” rather than client-side tracking, to avoid false positives and to cover SDK/non-SDK traffic.

Approach implemented:
1) Signal source
- Consume aggregated gateway request records from the existing metering/log pipeline (same dataset used for usage analytics), filtered to inference endpoints.
- Filter criteria:
  - project_id is present
  - route is one of supported inference endpoints OR route tagged inference=true in gateway routing metadata
  - status_code between 200–299
  - exclude internal/system traffic (service accounts) by credential_type != internal

2) State write
- On first observed success for (org_id, project_id), write:
  - step_id = FIRST_SUCCESSFUL_REQUEST
  - completed_at = min(timestamp)
  - completed_by = "validator:first_successful_request"
  - source = "gateway"
- Use UPSERT with a unique constraint on (org_id, project_id, step_id) to guarantee idempotency.

3) Lag / freshness
- Validator runs on a 2-minute schedule and queries the last 30 minutes of gateway success records; plus a one-time backfill job for 30 days when feature flag is enabled for an org.
- Expected end-to-end lag: 2–8 minutes.

4) Streaming edge cases
- Streaming requests returning 200 are counted as a successful request for this step.
- The dedicated “first streaming session” step remains separate and is validated by streaming-specific signals (ENG-23114).

5) Privacy
- Persist only: org_id, project_id, completed_at, endpoint_group (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank), region, model_id (optional), and request_id (hashed) for debugging.
- Do not persist: prompt, response, headers containing auth, raw IP.

6) Telemetry
- Emit event when step flips to complete:
  - onboarding.step_completed
  - properties: step_id, org_id, project_id, completed_at, source, endpoint_group, model_id (if allowlisted)
- Ensure allowlist is enforced (ENG-23120 may tighten further post-review).

comments: 2026-01-23 (Nadia Rahman): Please ensure the completion event uses the v1 schema names (onboarding.step_completed) and that model_id is only included if it’s already in the allowlist. No raw request_id in telemetry—hash if needed for internal logs only.

2026-01-24 (Amara Diallo): For status filtering, confirm that gateway returns 200 for streaming even if the client disconnects. If we see 200 with near-zero bytes, we might still mark complete; that’s okay for “first request”, but don’t let it satisfy “streaming session”.

2026-01-28 (Chloe Martin): State writes must be per project and should not require Console page view. Also, please add a backfill path so existing projects don’t get stuck incomplete when they already used the API before seeing the checklist.

2026-02-03 (Marcus Lin): Privacy reminder: do not store request/response bodies. Ensure any debug logging is behind an internal-only flag and redact auth-related headers/fields. Retention tag should follow onboarding telemetry policy.

2026-02-12 (Mei Lin): For dashboards, we need a stable completed_at timestamp and a clear source dimension (gateway vs client). Please include endpoint_group to break down which endpoint most users hit first.
